title: First Canadian Place
status: Source authoring in progress; no visual, geographic or maximum-fidelity approval

imagesInspected.notes: Dusk exterior: horizontal white spandrels, dark recessed corner strip, high BMO identity panel and rooftop aerials.

Construction photograph: larger new spandrels above rig and small original marble pieces below. Wide new panels align with pairs of narrower vision lights. Do not model the temporary suspended rig as permanent building geometry.
Comparative montage includes an altered after image. Useful for design intent, not independent as-built roof/site evidence.

facts: Project dated 2012; 72 storeys.
White custom fritted glass replaced the original marble; the public retail podium was also renovated.
Reports 5,370 spandrel panels, which differs from the executive architect's count; do not derive the facade layout from this total alone.

references.role: Architect of record and design collaborator
facts: Completed 2012.
Over 5,600 white glass and bronze panels replaced 45,000 marble panels.
Re-entrant corners use tinted glass.

Page 30 compares old small marble joints with larger new spandrels. Page 31 identifies the triangular frit option selected. Page 33 shows flush broad panels, thinner retaining trims and the existing window band beneath.
Page 37 text reports 5,625 fritted panels and 80 panels per floor; retain the differing counts as source-specific quantities.
references.caution: Several illustrations are design alternatives or renderings. Do not treat them all as executed geometry.

facts: Level 27 is shown as a square-like plan with four re-entrant corners, a central core and regular perimeter column bays.
Published rentable area 29,185 square feet is not an exterior plan dimension. No dimensioned outline is visible in this sheet.

references.role: Halsall project presentation, Building Science symposium, July 30, 2012
facts: Page 43 shows the typical facade section, corner return and closure trims; its embedded dimension text is not legible at the inspected resolution.
Page 47 shows large prefabricated glass spandrel panels and layered glass construction.
Text identifies separate face/corner marble populations and retained window assemblies, so the model must distinguish cladding from vision glazing.
Text on PDF page 56 gives approximately 9 ft from structural slab to suspended ceiling, not the floor-to-floor height.
Interior tenant-door standards must not be used to infer the building's street entrances.
Two principal guyed lattice masts and a smaller central pole, multiple antenna/dish assemblies and a rooftop equipment enclosure are visible.
The crown has a wide white glass band with BMO identity panels.

facts: White triangular frit panels, narrow metallic joints, glossy wall panels, a deep colonnade, overhead rectangular light openings, granite skirting and cylindrical bollards are visible.
references.caution: Image is linked, not redistributed or used as a texture. Exact street-level layout and dimensions remain to be registered.

currentReview.scope: The unchanged four-part GPU-instanced firstCanadianPlaceStudy.encodeAssembly remains the detailed source master. Runtime close-up reproduces all original geometry while combining opaque vision, bronze and backing surfaces into one tinted glass group. Six canonical graphs remain distinct for white fritted glass, stainless steel, painted metal, concrete, granite paving and marble lobby walls; with opaque and 52 percent clear palette glass this deliberately uses eight near groups, preserving visibly different architectural finishes rather than duplicating bitmaps. The preserved master has ten groups. Street retains every original office stripe and BMO vector mark, with a simpler recessed glazed lobby, whole piers and six-sided bollards; roof lattice stages, antennas and plant louvres are reduced. District retains each office stripe and all four corner steps, with sparse piers, closed mast envelopes and the round emblem in place of small wordmark strokes. Skyline merges five floor intervals into broad white/vision bands with the same area ratio; texture means are baked into one palette draw and small details are omitted. All levels retain the closed notched slab, crown, plant enclosure and three distinct masts. Owner modules, reconstructed 289.9 m body parapet, 298.1 m plant top, 355 m north tip and 351 m reconstructed south tip remain distinct. Average office spacing extrapolates floor datums; it does not survey every slab or confirm the allocation of marketed floor labels. Facade panel counts differ across publications, and the 50 mm triangular frit pitch is inferred. Exact door inventory, roof aerial layout and approximate BMO lettering are reconstructions. The model extent is the tower and its recessed colonnade within the mapped tower envelope; the broader retail/Exchange Tower complex is a separate site model and is excluded. Public raw adjacent outlines do not establish a surveyed retail boundary. Grade is approximate and no footprint replacement is used. Physical device and dense-city timing measurements remain pending.
currentReview.placement: Fresh raw Q1052475 way 27767627 matches the independently preserved ground outline within 0.002 m projection rounding. Anchor [-79.381691573,43.648765146] and heading 0.277301287909 remain fixed: native +X ENE at 74.112 degrees and +Z SSE at 164.112 degrees. Actually inspected owner north-annotated level-27 plan supports the four corner recesses and independently inferred 190 ft by 180 ft office envelope. The original photographer labels the 355 m north mast and supplies a view from the geographically southwest CN Tower; that actual photograph shows the tall open northern lattice and shorter white-topped southern mast, signing the north/south rooftop allocation independently of the map rectangle. The model places those at [-7,-19] and [-7,19], with the shorter center mast [7,0]. Exact mast offsets and secondary tip height remain reconstructed. Street approaches and pier spacing are reconstructed within the tower envelope, not a surveyed entrance inventory. The fresh map also includes wider office outlines 61429747 and 366222382, but neither labels a complete measured FCP retail podium: one has layer 5 and the other an explicit subdivision warning. Those wider site masses are excluded from this tower asset rather than stretching the tower to them. Mapped 292 m is retained separately from registry architecture 298.1 m, tip 355 m and highest occupied floor 287.1 m; body parapet 289.9 m is the photographer working datum. Y0 is approximate entrance grade, without surveyed pavement slope. No footprint replacement.
